target_customer: Restaurant and hospitality employers hiring hourly frontline workers, later broader frontline employers
problem: Hourly roles in restaurants and hospitality have very high turnover, and employers lack a fast, mobile way to find and hire workers.
business_model: B2B hiring platform sold to employers, with a worker-side mobile app
product_category: Frontline worker hiring marketplace, now generative AI hiring

founders.name: Vivian Wang
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch (2022-04-07) says she worked on the corporate team at Gap Inc., advising executives on workforce management strategy, and founded Landed in March 2020 in the Bay Area. Education not found. The YC page lists her as the only founder.

investors: founders of Warby Parker, Harry's and Allbirds' Good Friends fund

competitors.name: Fountain
competitors.what: Applicant tracking and hiring automation for hourly and gig roles
competitors.traction_then: Reported over one million applications a month for 150,000 hourly and gig roles

competitors.name: Instawork
competitors.what: On-demand hourly staffing marketplace for hospitality and events
competitors.funding_then: $30M from Spark Capital, Benchmark and Burst Capital

technical_complexity.rationale: A two-sided mobile and web matching product with standard engineering; the hard part was supply and demand growth, not technology. Generative AI features came years later.

defensibility.rationale: Hourly hiring tools were numerous and copyable; any lock-in came from employer integrations and worker pool size, which were still small in the early years.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Well-funded hourly hiring players already existed; no incumbent acquired or copied Landed as far as found. TechCrunch in 2022 named Seasoned, Fountain, Workstream and Bite Ninja as rivals.

market_need_then: Restaurant and hospitality turnover was a widely reported cost; TechCrunch 2021 quotes the founder drawing on high hourly turnover she saw at Gap. The pandemic then made hourly hiring more urgent.

branding.domain_note: Uses gotlanded.com rather than landed.com; the plain name is taken by other companies, for example a down payment assistance firm.

identity.logo: Lowercase 'landed' wordmark style in press releases
identity.voice_and_tone: Direct and upbeat; the company calls itself a hiring platform built for the frontline workforce

brand_strength.rationale: Generic word shared with other companies, no sourced press about the brand itself, domain needs a prefix.

outcome_analysis: Landed is still active. It launched a mobile app and raised a $1.4M seed in February 2021 and a $7M seed in April 2022 from Javelin and others, and now positions itself as an AI hiring platform for frontline workers, with a 2025 Inc. 5000 listing per search results. No Series A was verified, so the company sits in a long seed stage in a crowded hourly hiring field.
notes: YC lists founding 2019 and batch Winter 2019, but TechCrunch says Landed was founded in March 2020, a conflict not resolved. Aggregators (Wellfound $15.3M total, CB Insights $8.4M) disagree; two Series A entries on aggregators appear to belong to a different company and were not recorded. Competitors are dated Nov 2019, the closest dated source to the batch. The seed round of 2021 is labelled seed by TechCrunch.
